purpose: This is the paid-ad script writer and gate that runs after the Hook Lab and before any voice, lyric, storyboard or render. It has five modes: WRITE, GRADE, FIX, LADDER and LEARN. A script is treated as a chain of beliefs. The steps are: brief and persona cards, a length router (D15 to V300), a structure library (ST1 to ST18), a pre-write pack (a 14-rung belief ladder with the because test, a question chain, a six-sheet script bible and a reveal plan), 2 or 3 spines, writing as speech under 12 rules, then a line table. The gate is 16 mechanical tests plus a 24-question lessons list, a cold read by a fresh agent (a second, skeptical reader from S90 up) and a 100-point score. A script releases at 85 or more with no critical fail, after at most 3 FIX loops, then it escalates to the user. Six format adapters cover animation, song, podcast, UGC, text on screen and VSL. LEARN maps Meta ad drop-offs to lines. Appendix X holds the model scripts X1 to X8, Appendix R the research basis, and Appendix M the Copy Laws, which is the single copy for the whole Readymerce system. The skill makes no images, video or audio and has no render settings. It is a script and copy gate only.

phases.name: Mode and call contract (section 0)
phases.does: The caller picks WRITE / GRADE / FIX / LADDER / LEARN and passes one SCRIPT LAB CALL block: mode, brief card, format adapter (animation / song / podcast / ugc / text / vsl), length tier or "route it", structure code ST1 to ST18 per tier or "pick it", hook stacks (master + 2 variants with seam lines), cast and measured pace, script (GRADE/FIX), ad IDs plus line tables with voice timestamps (LEARN). Returns the release block (section 13).
phases.gate: Block complete. If the skill can't be loaded, the caller uses the Script Lab card (section 20) "and says so". Any change to a released script goes back through the gate.

phases.name: Brief card and persona card (2a, 2b)
phases.does: Brief card: one avatar, starting belief quoted with research ID, target belief, desire (LF8), awareness/sophistication stamp, angle, her material, mechanism (UMP/UMS), the picture, product truth, offer facts, proof facts, structure, adapter and cast, hook stacks. Persona card: only what she knows and believes before the ad, including patience ("you give an ad 3 seconds"). Skeptic variant from S90 up.
phases.gate: 3+ accommodations, 3+ moments, 3+ failed fixes, each with a research ID. A missing fact means the line is cut or rewritten, never invented. The persona card never holds the cause, mechanism, picture or its name, product, angle or the ad's purpose.

phases.name: Length router (section 3)
phases.does: Pick the job by awareness (demo / conversation / story), then the tier D15, D30, C45, S60, S90, L150 or V300, and turn it into a word ceiling at the measured pace (pre-cast 2.5 to 3 words/s, about 2.4 for savouring characters). Split the ceiling across the tier template's beats before writing.
phases.gate: No story under 55 s. Every concept gets a short tier (D30 or C45) and a story tier (S60 or S90), each written on its own and never trimmed. L150/V300 need a stated reason. Never speed the voice past 1.05x: cut a rung or move up a tier. Podcast C45 uses 35 to 45 s and 80 to 110 words.
phases.tools_models: cast voice's measured pace from the caller's casting step

phases.name: Structure pick (section 3b)
phases.does: Three layers in order: structure (ST1 to ST18), then device (narrator, confession, mentor, talking organ, villain, two hosts, creator, founder, cards, song), then medium (format adapter). Pick by awareness, then the load-bearing rung, the tier and the facts on hand. Writes a STRUCTURE PICK block. AIDA and 4Ps are lenses only.
phases.gate: The facts the structure needs must be on the facts sheet, or the structure is dropped (never invent a case, quote, competitor claim or deadline). Spines use at least 2 structures when awareness allows more than one. A story structure never runs under 55 s. From S60 up, every structure keeps one person, one moment and the accommodation.

phases.name: Pre-write pack (sections 4 to 7)
phases.does: Belief ladder, rungs 0 Curiosity to 13 Identity, with a because sentence for every adjacent pair. Question chain: a master question plus section and line questions, with loop rules. Script bible of six sheets: speakers/POV, one timeline, picture map with a product row, word list, setups/payoffs, facts. Reveal plan in fixed order: carrier with a reason, shown working, bridge line, each part's job, how to use; named after it is shown and after the mechanism.
phases.gate: Every because sentence holds. The six fixed points hold: cause before promise, promise before mechanism, mechanism before the product's name, explanation before claim, proof right after its claim, offer before CTA. The master question opens by the end of the hook (about 3 to 8 s) with no line between hook and CTA lacking an open question. Re-hooks come about every 8 s early, then every 25 to 30 s. One picture, and the product obeys its rules. Every fact is sourced.

phases.name: Spines (section 8)
phases.does: Write 2 or 3 spines of about 80 words each (tier, job, structure and device, entry to final rung, story shape, hook, master question, ladder, carrier and reveal, picture, payoff, why). Pick one and write only that one at each tier of its ladder.
phases.gate: Spines must differ in something that matters: structure, entry rung, carrier, story shape or hook type.
phases.human_checkpoint: "Pick one. The calling skill's gate decides; when the user has said to run without stopping, Claude picks and says why in one line." (line 408)

phases.name: Write it as speech: 12 rules plus tier templates (sections 9, 10)
phases.does: One block of speech, top to bottom, inside the word budget, then read aloud at the voice's pace. The 12 rules: one of each; one job per line; every line owes the next an answer (but/so/that's why); manage the loops; picture first, then the science; fixed order; the mechanism explains why the old fixes failed; the product walks in through the story; explain every new word and frame every quote; every payoff has a setup in the same words; one timeline with facts from the sheet; write for the ear. Tier templates give per-beat word budgets.
phases.gate: Core lines under 12 words, none over 17. Grade 7 or below. Contractions. At most one "it's not X, it's Y" line, at the aha. Past tense for the story, present for the mechanism, with the switch marked.

phases.name: Line table (section 11)
phases.does: Built from the speech. Columns: # | Speaker | Line | Job | Answers | Opens | Picture | Gap | Words | Time. Time starts as a word-count estimate and is replaced by real voice timestamps once the voiceover exists.
phases.gate: One job per line. Answers/Opens are blank only on the last line.

phases.name: Gate part A: 16 mechanical tests plus the lessons list (12A, 19)
phases.does: Tests: 1 ladder coverage, 2 ladder order (because test, fixed points, structure order), 3 handoffs, 4 master loop, 5 speaker/POV, 6 timeline and facts, 7 words (explained before used), 8 picture map, 9 setups/payoffs, 10 deletion and repetition, 11 reveal order, 12 hook seam/payoff/no clickbait (every variant stack), 13 ear, 14 length arithmetic, 15 strategy minimum, 16 Copy Law essentials (L22 script items). Then the 24 yes/no lessons; a "no" fails the mapped test.
phases.gate: Each test is pass/fail with line numbers and quotes as evidence. Stacks that fail test 12 go back to the Hook Lab (H6) or move to a tier whose body pays them.

phases.name: Gate part B: cold read (12B)
phases.does: A fresh general-purpose agent per read, never one that has seen the brief, research or an earlier draft or read. It gets only the persona card and the numbered spoken lines, labelled "Voice 1"/"Voice 2". It writes a per-line table (what's going on, question, wait who/what/when, still watching), a 5-sentence retell, the doubt left, would you tap, and the single most confusing moment. A second skeptic reader runs from S90 up. The read is listen-only; supers, end card and primary text are graded by the format's sound-off test.
phases.gate: Pass when the retell matches the ladder rung by rung, there is no confusion on a core rung (cause, mechanism, product, why it works, offer) left uncleared within 2 lines, and there is no scroll point before the master answer (stories) or before the product is seen working (demos). If no agent can be started: "cold read: self, weaker check".
phases.tools_models: Agent tool (general-purpose) per reader; new readers every loop

phases.name: Gate part C: 100-point score and FIX loops (12C, 12D)
phases.does: Score: Comprehension 25, Ladder and handoffs 20, Hook 10, Mechanism 10, Proof 10, Offer and CTA 10, Emotion and identity 5, Ear 5, Length 5. Then the gate report.
phases.gate: Release at 85 or more with no critical fail. Critical fails: a major confusion on a core rung; a required rung missing; a speaker or timeline break; an invented or unsourced fact. Up to 3 rewrite loops, each with new readers.
phases.human_checkpoint: After loop 3, ESCALATE: "the script goes to the user with the remaining fails named and the writer's recommendation" (line 642)
phases.tools_models: Agent tool for new cold readers per loop

phases.name: Release and changes after release (section 13)
phases.does: Release block: 1 clean script in the adapter's line format, 2 line table, 3 pre-write pack (structure pick, ladder and because sentences, question chain, six bible sheets, reveal plan, spines), 4 gate report, 5 length ladder, 6 hooks sent back.
phases.gate: Any later change goes through FIX on the changed lines and re-runs tests 3, 5 to 10, 13 and 14 with the bible updated. A core-rung change (cause, mechanism, reveal, offer) re-runs the full gate with a new cold reader. No un-gated change reaches voice, song, storyboard or render.
phases.human_checkpoint: none in the skill. Legal: "The brand's legal team decides what passes" (line 17)

phases.name: GRADE mode (section 14)
phases.does: Number the lines one breath each, rebuild the bible from the script, infer the brief (avatar, awareness, angle, job, tier from the word count, structure; "none: a list of beats" is a finding), build the line table, run the 16 tests, lessons, cold read(s) and score. Report breaks ranked by damage with a one-line fix each. Don't rewrite unless asked.
phases.gate: Same gate. For swipes, test 6 checks internal consistency only; name 1 or 2 moves worth stealing.

phases.name: FIX mode (section 15)
phases.does: List the failing lines and tests. Sort each into a line break (fix the line) or a structure break (rebuild from the spine section by section; a weak bridge is never patched with one line). Update the bible first, keep the word budget, re-run the full gate with new readers and count the loop.
phases.gate: 85 with no critical fail. Max 3 loops.
phases.human_checkpoint: Escalate to the user after loop 3 (line 697)

phases.name: LADDER mode (section 16)
phases.does: From the released spine, each new tier gets its own structure, beats, a hook stack whose seam fits the new line 2, and new bridges inside the new budget.
phases.gate: Never trim (a short version keeping the long version's bridges fails test 3). Gate each tier on its own.

phases.name: LEARN mode (section 17)
phases.does: After about 7 days or 1,000+ impressions per ad, pull read-only Meta metrics. Map the 3 steepest falls after 3 s, plus falls at joins, to lines via the voice timestamps. Diagnose: a drop before 15 s is the hook or seam; a cliff at product entry is the bridge; a good hold with low CTR is the offer, CTA or bridge. Keep 1 or 2 deep lessons per ad as yes/no questions in section 19 with ad ID and date. Confused comments become cold-read prompt questions; comments go to VOC docs; an angle gets 3 to 6 executions.
phases.gate: Deep lessons only (causes, not features), each labelled research, execution or feedback-loop. Cost per purchase at ad-set level decides.

phases.name: Adapter: animation
phases.does: One line = one breath = one picture, 4 to 17 words. Line format `SPEAKER (delivery note) [gap code]: text`, gaps S 0.15 s / B 0.4 s / H 0.8 s. Commas join running thoughts because TTS stops at full stops. TTS-safe numbers and phonetic brand spelling, with acting tags in brackets. A character's "I" holds until a marked switch. The picture note feeds the shot ledger and the picture map feeds the Invisible-Made-Visible sequence.
phases.gate: Brand name at least twice, the first only after the product is shown. Cold read on the voiceover lines only; supers checked by the animation skill's sound-off test.

phases.name: Adapter: song
phases.does: Script Lab writes the argument as speech (C45, S60 or S90) and gates it. The song skill turns it into lyrics: the chorus carries the picture and its name; the turn, guarantee and CTA are spoken. Script Lab then grades the lyrics read flat.
phases.gate: Tests 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 12, 13 on the lyrics (every line understood first listen, 8 to 14 syllables allowed), plus a cold read of the lyrics. Every rung, fact and time word unchanged vs the released speech (tests 1, 6), identity close kept (test 16). Length about 35 to 55 lines per 90 s, aiming at the tier's low end because Suno runs 10 to 25 s long.

phases.name: Adapter: podcast and conversations
phases.does: The C45 template is the podcast beat template (Host A owns the problem, Host B has solved it). Both hosts go on the speaker sheet and the cold reader hears Voice 1/Voice 2. The long cut L150 is its own script.
phases.gate: 8 to 12 turns, 80 to 110 spoken words, 35 to 45 s (test 14 counts against this). Turns of 20 words or fewer (one up to 25). The listener speaks every other turn and at least every 8 s. No host over 60% of words. Brand line one casual sentence of 25 words or fewer. Payoff ends on 6 words or fewer. CTA off the voice; offer and CTA scored on end card, supers and primary text.

phases.name: Adapter: UGC and talking head
phases.does: One creator, first person, present tense for the routine and past for the story. Clip packing (hub G4) at natural pauses.
phases.gate: Up to about 35 words per 15-second clip, never splitting a line. Product working on camera from about 3 s for aware audiences. Supers 2 to 6 words, never the transcript.

phases.name: Adapter: text on screen and story text
phases.does: Each card is a line; the cold reader reads the cards in order. Primary text carries what the cards can't. Long-form native story ads keep the hub's B16 tests.
phases.gate: 12 words or fewer per card, one job per card.

phases.name: Adapter: VSL and long form (L150, V300)
phases.does: Chapters each end on a question. The loop device runs about 3 times. A mentor or authority explains in reported speech. The product enters unnamed and is shown working first.
phases.gate: CTA at about 3 and 5 min, looping back into proof. Every "true story" fact-checked before release.

story_structures.name: Full direct-response stack
story_structures.shape: Call-out: one person, one moment (1) · agitate: the accommodation and its cost (2) · failed fixes, each killed with its reason (3) · hidden cause, UMP (4) · promise (5) · how it gets fixed, UMS (6) · product carried in, shown, bridged, named (7) · proof (8) · ease (9) · offer (10) · risk reversal (11) · reason for now (12) · CTA · identity close (13). Tiers S90, L150, V300.
story_structures.organic_fit: Weak as is: three of its rungs (offer, risk reversal, now) are paid-only. It can be trimmed to rungs 1 to 9 plus 13 as a 60 to 90 s 'full breakdown' reel. Example: a Tirana clinic owner who boosts posts, why boosting failed, the hidden cause (slow replies), the fix (a reply system), a real client result, identity close ("owners who answer first are the ones who get booked"). CTA: comment a keyword for the reply checklist.

story_structures.name: PAS: problem, agitate, solve
story_structures.shape: The problem in her words (1) · agitate: the cost (2) · the cause in one plain line (4) · the product as the fix, with a bridge line (7) · the lived payoff (8) · CTA (12). Tiers C45, S60. Model X4.
story_structures.organic_fit: Strong for 30 to 45 s reach reels. Example: "I post every day and nobody messages" → what it costs (empty Tuesdays) → cause in one line ("your posts answer questions nobody in Tirana is asking") → the method, not the agency, as the fix → lived payoff. CTA: save or send to a business partner. Watch the 'no story under 55 s' rule: keep it a problem demo, not a mini story.

story_structures.name: Hidden cause ("this is why...")
story_structures.shape: An odd fact or an outside scene (0) · "that's me" (1) · the hidden cause, with the picture (4) · why her fixes missed it (3) · promise (5) · mechanism (6) · product (7) · proof (8) · offer, CTA. Tiers S60, S90, L150. Model X5.
story_structures.organic_fit: One of the best organic formats: curiosity-led and shareable. Example: "This is why your ads get likes but no DMs." Odd fact (most DMs in Albania arrive after 9 pm), then the hidden cause shown as one picture (a shop with the lights off when customers knock), then why boosting and posting more missed it, then the mechanism. The product can stay implicit ("how we set this up for clients"). CTA: follow for the series, or comment a keyword.

story_structures.name: Discovery story (epiphany bridge; star, story, solution)
story_structures.shape: Her life and the wall she hit (1, 2) · what she tried (3) · the carrier and the moment it clicked (4) · the new way (6, 7) · the result she can see (8) · offer and guarantee (10, 11) · identity, in her voice (13). Tiers S90, L150, V300. Models X6, X7, X8.
story_structures.organic_fit: This is the 'POV: a day in the life of the buyer with their pains, then the mechanism revealed' format. Device: first-person confession or the Diary register. Example: a restaurant owner's day from 7 am posting to 11 pm answering WhatsApps, the wall (a full competitor across the street), fixes tried (a nephew running Instagram, boosting), the carrier (a friend or our strategist) and the click (the cause), the new way, the visible result, identity close in her voice. Cut the offer and guarantee and end on a keyword or follow CTA. Script Lab routes it to S90 (80 to 100 s), but the organic adapter says reach reels run 30 to 60 s, so it needs an S60 organic variant or a 2-part series.

story_structures.name: Two futures
story_structures.shape: Two people, one difference (0 or 1) · what the difference is: the cause (4) · how to be the second one (6, 7) · proof (8) · CTA, identity (13). Tiers S60, S90.
story_structures.organic_fit: Strong for B2B, and split-screen friendly. Example: "Two dental clinics on the same street in Tirana. One is full on Tuesdays." The difference is the cause (reply speed, or posts that answer patient questions), then how to be the second clinic, then a real case as proof, then identity. CTA: send it to the clinic owner you know, or follow.

story_structures.name: Myth buster ("stop doing X")
story_structures.shape: The belief or habit she holds (3) · why it's wrong: the real cause (4) · what works instead (5, 6) · product (7) · proof (8) · CTA. Tiers D30, C45, S60. Model X3.
story_structures.organic_fit: Excellent at 20 to 45 s for reach and sends. Example: "Stop boosting posts." Why it fails (it buys likes from people who will never book), what works instead, the method or tool, proof. CTA: save, or send to a partner. Product naming is optional.

story_structures.name: Mistakes countdown
story_structures.shape: "[N] reasons your [X] isn't working" · each mistake with why it fails, escalating (3) · the last one is the real cause (4) · the fix (6, 7) · proof, CTA. Tiers C45, S60.
story_structures.organic_fit: A strong save driver that converts directly into a carousel (carousel-machine 'Count list'). Example: "3 reasons your Instagram brings followers but not clients." The list must escalate (Script Lab's swap test), and the last item is the real cause. CTA: save, or comment a keyword for the full list.

story_structures.name: Old way vs new way
story_structures.shape: Why the usual solution fails (3) · the new mechanism (4, 6) · the product as the easy way to get it (7) · proof (8) · offer, CTA. Tiers D30, C45, S60, S90. Model X6 lines 8 to 15.
story_structures.organic_fit: Natural for showing the agency's own comment-to-DM funnel. Old way: "post and wait for DMs". New way: "comment a word, get the answer in your inbox in seconds". The product (the DM bot) is shown as the easy way. The CTA can be a live demo: "comment PLAN and watch it happen". Drop the offer.

story_structures.name: Contrarian plus a named method
story_structures.shape: "[X] isn't the problem" (3) · the named method and its picture (4, 6) · its steps, each with a job (6, 7) · proof (8) · CTA. Tiers S60, S90. Explicitly for 'services, B2B, coaching'; sophistication 4 to 5.
story_structures.organic_fit: The best native B2B fit, and it mirrors carousel-machine's 'Contrarian plus named framework'. Example: "More followers isn't your problem", then a named method ("the 3-Reply Rule") with one picture, each step with its job, a real client proof, and a keyword CTA for the framework PDF. It also builds the agency's IP across a series.

story_structures.name: Comparison (us vs them)
story_structures.shape: The one thing she cares about most (1 or 5) · each alternative on that one thing (3) · the product on it (7) · proof (8) · offer, CTA. Tiers D15, D30, C45.
story_structures.organic_fit: Usable as 'agency vs freelancer vs doing it yourself' on one criterion (for example, who answers a DM at 10 pm). It needs real facts about the alternatives and should avoid naming local competitors. CTA: save, or comment a keyword. Medium fit.

story_structures.name: Case study
story_structures.shape: The situation (1) · the diagnosis (4) · what changed (6, 7) · the numbers (8) · the lesson, as identity (13) · CTA. Tiers C45, S60, S90. 'Problem aware for services'.
story_structures.organic_fit: A high-trust B2B format: a real Albanian client, the diagnosis, what changed, the numbers (from the facts sheet only, never invented), and the lesson as identity. CTA: comment CASE for the breakdown, or follow for the next case. It requires a documented case (Script Lab's facts rule).

story_structures.name: Skeptic testimony ("I was skeptical")
story_structures.shape: Her doubt, in her words (3) · why she tried it anyway (7) · what surprised her (8) · the result (8) · CTA. Tiers D30, C45, S60.
story_structures.organic_fit: A client on camera: "I thought agencies just post pretty pictures." It needs real client words and consent. UGC or talking-head device. CTA: follow, or DM. Good for trust posts.

story_structures.name: Objection crusher
story_structures.shape: The top fear, said out loud in her words · the blunt, honest answer (9 or 11) · proof (8) · offer (10) · CTA. Tiers D15, D30, C45.
story_structures.organic_fit: Works as an FAQ series of 15 to 30 s founder answers. Example: "Do I need to pay for ads to get clients from Instagram?" Blunt answer, proof, then replace the offer with a keyword or DM CTA. Cards-on-screen device works (12 words per card).

story_structures.name: Demo
story_structures.shape: The angle hook with the product working (1 or 5) · what it is (7) · an objection answered by showing (8, 9) · proof (8) · offer, CTA. Tiers D15, D30. Models X1, X2.
story_structures.organic_fit: A screen-recorded demo of a comment triggering an instant DM, working on screen by about 3 s, then an objection shown ("it answers in Albanian too"), then proof. CTA: "comment DEMO to try it". Drop the risk reversal.

story_structures.name: Offer first
story_structures.shape: The deal (10) · what's in it (7, 9) · the guarantee (11) · the real deadline (12) · CTA. Tiers D15, D30. Most aware.
story_structures.organic_fit: Poor fit for organic with no price or offer. Usable only for a free resource or free audit with a real deadline ("10 free audits this month") and a keyword CTA. Otherwise drop it from the organic library.

story_structures.name: Before, after, bridge
story_structures.shape: Life now: the accommodation (1, 2) · life after: the payoff scene (5) · the bridge: cause, mechanism, product (4, 6, 7) · proof (8) · CTA. Tiers C45, S60, S90.
story_structures.organic_fit: Good for account transformations ("before: 3 DMs a month; after: ..."), with real numbers only. Owner's accommodation ("I stopped checking Instagram because nothing came"), then the payoff scene, then the bridge. CTA: save, or keyword.

story_structures.name: Challenge timeline
story_structures.shape: "What happens if she does [X] for 30 days" (0) · day by day, with the honest dip (8) · why it worked (4, 6) · the product, shown from day 1, named after why (7) · offer, CTA. Tiers S60, S90, L150. Animation F4.
story_structures.organic_fit: An excellent episodic series with a natural 'follow for day N' CTA. Example: "What happens if a Tirana clinic answers every DM within 5 minutes for 30 days", with an honest dip and real tracked data only. It can also split into daily short reels.

story_structures.name: QUEST
story_structures.shape: Qualify: one person, one moment (1) · understand her life and her fixes (2, 3) · educate: cause, promise, mechanism (4, 5, 6) · stimulate: the future she gets and the proof (8) · transition to the offer (7, 10 to 13). Tiers L150, V300.
story_structures.organic_fit: Too long for reels (L150/V300). Usable for YouTube or long-form, or split into a 3 to 5 part reel series (qualify, understand, educate, stimulate) with a follow CTA.

story_structures.name: Story shape: failed-solution journey (Appendix M)
story_structures.shape: "I tried rosemary oil, then supplements, then my GP said it's hormonal." (does the objection work)
story_structures.organic_fit: Owner POV: "I tried a nephew, then a freelancer, then boosting", each failure with its reason, leading to the real cause. Good inside ST4 or ST6.

story_structures.name: Story shape: discovery (Appendix M)
story_structures.shape: "I found out why it happens at the part first." (does the mechanism work)
story_structures.organic_fit: The core of the POV-then-mechanism format: "I found out why my DMs die after 9 pm."

story_structures.name: Story shape: transformation with a witness (Appendix M)
story_structures.shape: "My sister noticed before I did." (this is the proof)
story_structures.organic_fit: "My receptionist noticed the phone stopped ringing before I did", or the reverse after the fix. Proof from a witness, with no paid-offer close needed.

story_structures.name: Story shape: confession (Appendix M)
story_structures.shape: "I stopped parting it in the middle a year ago. I never told anyone." (this is the problem)
story_structures.organic_fit: "I stopped posting our prices because nobody booked anyway." A strong cold-open hook for B2B owners. Accommodation-first (Copy Law 10).

story_structures.name: Registers: UGC / documentary / diary (Appendix M)
story_structures.shape: The same angle in three voices: UGC ("That's the crazy part."), documentary (third-person observation), diary ("I stopped ... today. I didn't decide to.")
story_structures.organic_fit: Variant volume for one organic concept. The diary register suits POV day-in-the-life reels, documentary suits a founder voice-over on b-roll of Tirana businesses, and UGC suits client testimonials.

story_structures.name: Two-host conversation (Mardyos clinic podcast, Tirana)
story_structures.shape: L1 A accommodation and cost · L2 B recognition pull · L3 A stakes · L4 B cause in one picture line · L5 A carried question · L6 B recognition and failed fix · L7 A pull · L8 B discovery, casual brand line · L9 A pull for result · L10 B lived payoff mirroring L1 ("And I sleep."). 8 to 12 turns, 80 to 110 words, 35 to 45 s.
story_structures.organic_fit: Already an Albanian B2B example (a clinic answering WhatsApps at 11 pm). A podcast-clip reel works organically as is. Swap the off-voice offer end card for a keyword or follow end card, and keep the brand line to one casual sentence.

story_structures.name: Device: villain mocking the fixes
story_structures.shape: Carries ST6, ST7, ST8. Mock the fix, never her.
story_structures.organic_fit: "The Boost Post button" or "the algorithm" as a villain mocking an owner's fixes. Animated, funny and shareable. Needs an AI label if it is AI-generated (Script Lab has no such rule).

story_structures.name: Device: talking part or object
story_structures.shape: Carries ST2, ST3, ST17. Its "I" holds until a marked switch.

Add an 'organic' adapter and a growth-engine caller row.

Rungs 10 Value, 11 Safety and 12 Now (offer, guarantee, urgency) are paid rungs. For organic, replace them with one organic CTA rung (follow, save, send, comment keyword, DM) and redefine critical fail 2 ("a rung the tier requires is missing", line 639) per organic tier, or every organic script fails the gate.

Re-weight the scorecard's 'Offer, risk reversal and CTA' area (10 points: real pricing line 3, guarantee four properties 3, CTA four jobs 4, line 631). For organic, score CTA fit to the post's job (reach: follow/save/send; trust: keyword for a resource; convert: keyword/DM) and the CTA's jobs (action, what happens next such as "I'll DM you the checklist", effort, reason). Mark pricing and guarantee n/a.

Test 16 (Copy Law essentials) checks the guarantee's four properties, the CTA's four jobs, the L13 objection order and the identity close. For organic, mark the guarantee and 'not worth it / what if I'm wrong / later' objections n/a. Keep the accommodation-first problem, promise smaller than proof, and identity or lived-payoff close. Test 15's "Check the urgency is real" becomes n/a.

Reconcile the identity close with the organic adapter's ending. Script Lab wants "the close lands on identity tied to the mechanism (S60 and up)" (line 574). The organic adapter wants the payoff in the last 3 to 5 s and a loop back to the hook or a CTA that is the payoff's next step. Pick one rule per tier.

Length router: router rule 2 says "No story under 55 seconds", while the organic adapter says reach reels run 30 to 60 s. Decide whether organic story formats (ST4 POV day-in-the-life, ST3, ST17) ship at S60 (55 to 65 s) or split into a series. The 'every concept ships a short tier and a story tier' rule (line 78) is a paid testing rule; for organic, one tier per post is enough. Keep 'write each length on its own, never trim'.

Product reveal timing: problem-aware stories reveal at 50 to 60% of runtime, unaware at about 40 to 50 s, aware demos at about 3 s (line 391). In organic B2B posts the 'product' is usually the method or insight, and the agency may never be named, or only at the end ("how we do it for clients"). Keep the fixed order (mechanism before the name, shown before named), but let the reveal plan say 'method' when there is no product. Demos of the DM bot keep the 3 s rule.

Brief card: replace "Offer facts (from the live page): price lines, bundle, guarantee terms, real urgency" (line 98) with resource or keyword facts: the live keyword (only keywords marked live in the brain), what the DM delivers, and the series it belongs to. Proof facts stay facts-sheet only, with no invented client numbers.

Persona card and cold-read prompt are written for a female DTC buyer watching an ad: "you give an ad 3 seconds" (line 118), "An ad starts playing" (line 587), "Would you tap?" (line 605), retell sentence "what the product is". For organic B2B, use the owner persona (an Albanian clinic, restaurant or shop owner, scrolling at night), 'a reel starts playing in your feed', 'Would you follow / save / send / comment the keyword? Why?', and a retell sentence about the method.

Cold read mode: Script Lab's read is "listen-only" (line 617), with supers handed to "the format's sound-off test" in the calling skill. The organic adapter says the cold reader reads "sound off first". Add a sound-off read (captions and on-screen text only) as a second organic pass, because IG reels are often watched muted and no organic skill owns the sound-off test.

LEARN is Meta-ads-only: ad IDs, the Facebook Ads connector, link CTR, cost per purchase, "1,000 or more impressions per ad" (lines 708 to 711). Organic LEARN needs IG organic insights (plays, average watch time or retention where available, saves, shares, follows, keyword comments, DMs) keyed by post ID. Rewrite the C13-style diagnosis ("a good hold with a low CTR is the offer") as "a good hold with low saves, sends or follows is the payoff or CTA". No hedges, no 'may', no compliance notes", and line 18 frames risk as "will get the ad rejected by Meta". Organic posts skip Meta ad review, and small Albanian B2B clients have no legal team, so an organic reviewer must own claim checks (results only from the facts sheet, no guaranteed-outcome promises) and IG branded-content rules.

Hook rules: keep test 12 (seam, payoff, no clickbait; every variant stack checked against the body). Swap the Hook Lab's paid DTC tuning for a B2B profile upstream. Organic hooks can be result-first only in demo-type structures, matching Script Lab's own demo allowance.

Language and pace: the ear rules (contractions, grade 7, words/s) are English-calibrated. Albanian scripts need their own measured pace before budgeting (router rule 8), and the TTS-safe rules (numbers as words, phonetic brand spelling) apply to Albanian names.

Structure library mapping: the organic adapter's list (problem-solution, breakdown, case study, list, tutorial, myth vs truth, tier list, 'never ever', borrowed interest, personal story) should map to ST codes so GRADE can name them: problem-solution = ST2, case study = ST11, list = ST7, myth vs truth = ST6, personal story = ST4 or ST16, breakdown = ST3 or ST9. Appendix M admits the gap: "The nine beats are a direct-response argument. They have no organic front or discovery carrier." (line 1588). The organic version needs a discovery-first front such as a value-per-second check or lock-in zone (which the organic adapter adds).
visual_qa_overlap:
Script Lab does almost no visual QA. It makes no sheets, storyboards, frames, prompt cards or takes. What it does have:

1. The line table's Picture column, \"what is on screen (animation and video); in the picture map's words for mechanism lines\" (line 534).
2. The picture map (6c): one metaphor per script, with a product row that must obey the picture's rules.
3. The animation adapter's \"One line = one breath = one picture: 4 to 17 words, ending where a cut or a picture change can go\" (line 724). \"The picture note on each line feeds the shot ledger; the picture map feeds the Invisible-Made-Visible sequence\" (line 729).
4. Visual requirements stated as copy rules: the product is shown working before it is named (reveal plan); the product works on screen from about 3 s for aware audiences; the brand name is not voiced until after the product is shown; supers are 2 to 6 words and never the transcript; cards are 12 words or fewer.
5. The cold read deliberately strips visuals. The reader gets \"No delivery notes, no picture notes, no line table, no intent\" (line 583), and \"Supers, the end card and the primary text are graded separately (the format's sound-off test)\" (line 617). That test belongs to the calling skill, for example the animation skill.

Appendix M concedes the gap: \"He never covers how to write the visual track. Everything is copy.\" (line 1589).

What Script Lab offers a reviewer is a template: the fresh-agent pattern of 12B (a new agent per pass that sees only the persona and the artifact, never the brief or earlier drafts, with a per-item table, a retell and a pass rule).

What a fresh-agent Visual/Prompt/Take Reviewer would add:
- A sound-off cold read: frames plus captions only, mirroring the listen-only read.
- A per-line check that each storyboard frame or clip matches the line's Picture column and the picture map: one metaphor, no visual second metaphor, and the product's on-screen action obeys the picture's rule. Lesson 16's failure, where readers scrolled when the product broke the picture, has a visual twin.
- Reveal-order checks on frames: product shown before its name appears on screen or in supers; product on screen by about 3 s in demos; no brand on screen before it is shown working.
- Super and card checks: word counts, no transcript duplication, and the CTA end card (the organic keyword or follow instead of offer and price).
- Take-level checks that picture changes land on line ends and gap codes (S 0.15, B 0.4, H 0.8 s), using the Time column once voice timestamps exist.
- Prompt-card review, which Script Lab lacks entirely.

Any line a Take Reviewer changes in the edit must route back through Script Lab FIX (tests 3, 5 to 10, 13, 14), per \"A script never reaches the voice, the song, the storyboard or a render with an un-gated change\" (line 676).

costs.credits: No credit figures anywhere in the skill. Only "Scripts are cheap and renders are not: write every length the concept needs, render only the ones being tested." (line 78) and "Read-aloud pass on every script before any credits are spent." (line 1673)
Not priced. 1 fresh agent per loop (2 from S90 up), up to 3 loops. The acceptance WRITE run used "eleven cold reads over three loops" (line 791)
Not credits: "A 5-minute script is about 2 days of work." (line 1497)

other_issues: The per-beat word budgets don't add up to the tier ranges, though line 440 says "The budgets add up to the tier's range". Summing the tier templates: D15 beats 22 to 40 vs tier 30 to 45; D30 54 to 94 vs 70 to 100; C45 61 to 117 vs 100 to 140; S60 134 to 212 vs 140 to 190; S90 198 to 297 vs 210 to 280. An agent that fills every beat at its maximum can't reach the C45 or D15 ceiling, and at its minimum it fails every floor. Test 14 and the length score ("2 within 10% over") will disagree with the beat budgets.

Two C45 budgets: router 40 to 50 s and 100 to 140 words (line 136) vs podcast 35 to 45 s and 80 to 110 words (lines 150, 742). The Script Lab card (line 806), which the drama and podcast skills copy word for word, carries only the 40 to 50 s version.
